data.description:
# The completion gate cannot verify a large epic: step budget exhausts at 480 AND at 1600

## The failure

Closing epic [rebar:e369-a449-4773-48fb] (59 descendants, all closed and certified) fails:

    Error: cannot close e369-a449-4773-48fb: completion verification could not run
    (completion verification workflow did not produce a verdict: step 'decide@then/verify' failed:
     agent exceeded its step budget (max_iterations=480; ~1 model request per tool call).
     Raise REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS or narrow the task.)

Retried with `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=1600` (3.3x the default). **Exhausted again**, after ~50 minutes,
identical message, `max_iterations=1600`.

## Why two data points matter more than one

If this were merely "a big epic needs more room", tripling the budget should have finished a task that
got most of the way at 480. Exhausting at BOTH 480 and 1600 is the signature of **non-convergence**
rather than a budget slightly too small — but that is an inference, not a measurement, because the
failure emits no progress signal at all: no partial verdict, no count of tickets examined, no
indication of how far it got. **The gate cannot be tuned because it cannot be observed.**

## Why this is a gate DESIGN defect, not an environment problem

The error names two remedies — raise the budget, or "narrow the task". Neither is available to an
agent acting correctly:

* Raising is unbounded guesswork with no feedback, and each attempt costs ~50 minutes of live LLM time.
* There is no sanctioned way to narrow a completion verification by DESCENDANT COUNT. `--ref <sha>`
  retargets which tree is verified, not how many children are scanned.

So the only remaining documented escape is the one printed at the end of the same message:
`Override with --force-close="<reason>"`. **That is the trap.** A force-closed ticket is precisely the
unattested state epic e369 spent its whole cycle removing — it is why [rebar:b586-2fda-8a15-4260],
[rebar:0059-c7f0-cce1-4077] and [rebar:2bc7-...] were reopened. A gate whose only reachable exit under
load is the thing the project forbids will eventually be exited that way by someone in a hurry.

Same shape as the certification trap ([rebar:738a-376e-4829-42ca]): two individually correct rules
composing into a state with no honest exit.

## Evidence

* Epic e369: **59 descendants, 59 closed, 0 uncertified**, 14/14 acceptance criteria met, fresh
  plan-review attestation `certified`, exit bar verified on `main` (harness run 30986591446: 62 passed,
  0 failed, 0 errored). Nothing about the epic's readiness is in question — only the verifier's ability
  to finish evaluating it.
* Attempt 1: default `max_iterations=480` — exhausted.
* Attempt 2: `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=1600` — exhausted after ~50 min.
* Both failed at the same step: `decide@then/verify`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] the verifier's step usage on a large epic is MEASURED and reported — how many steps, spent on
      what — so the failure is diagnosable rather than a bare budget number
- [ ] it is established BY MEASUREMENT whether the verifier converges on a 59-descendant epic at any
      budget or loops; the two-exhaustion evidence above is suggestive, not conclusive
- [ ] a large epic can complete verification without an operator guessing an env var: either the work
      scales (e.g. child verdicts are reused rather than re-derived) or the budget is derived from
      descendant count
- [ ] the failure message stops offering `--force-close` as the de-facto remedy for a RESOURCE limit —
      a resource exhaustion is not a verdict, and conflating them steers agents into the unattested
      state the project forbids
- [ ] e369 closes through the gate with a genuine `completion-verifier` signature, not a force

## Testing

    rebar transition e369-a449-4773-48fb in_progress closed     # the reproduction
    pytest tests/unit -k completion -q
data.title: Completion gate cannot verify a 59-descendant epic: step budget exhausts at 480 and at 1600, leaving --force-close as the only exit
